harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), hardened /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev, made the settings persistent, verified enforcement, rebooted the node, and confirmed the hardening survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline mount/fstab state on node1
Created systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/tmp.mount.d/hardening.conf setting Options=mode=1777,strictatime,noexec,nosuid,nodev for tmp.mount
Ran daemon-reload, enabled and started tmp.mount so /tmp is a noexec,nosuid,nodev tmpfs mount
Added a /dev/shm entry to /etc/fstab with options defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec and remounted /dev/shm to apply immediately

Functionally verified noexec (script execution denied, exit 126), nosuid (setuid bit set but unusable since exec is blocked; nosuid flag present in mount options), and nodev (mknod'd device node exists but open/cat against it fails) on both /tmp and /dev/shm
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy mount/service state as baseline
Issued a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed and uptime was ~7.7s, proving an actual reboot occurred

Re-verified post-reboot that /tmp and /dev/shm are mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec, tmp.mount is active and enabled, the /etc/fstab entry for /dev/shm persisted, and the noexec enforcement test again returned exit 126 on both mounts

evidence.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persistent across reboot
evidence.summary: tmp.mount existed disabled with default options; a systemd drop-in set Options=...,noexec,nosuid,nodev, tmp.mount was enabled+started, mount output showed the new options applied, an exec test returned Permission denied/exit 126, and after reboot the mount options and enforcement were unchanged.

evidence.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persistent across reboot
evidence.summary: Added a /dev/shm line to /etc/fstab with nosuid,nodev,noexec, remounted it live to confirm application, verified exec was blocked, and after reboot the fstab entry and enforcement persisted.

evidence.requirement: setuid bits are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: Both filesystems mount with the nosuid flag confirmed in mount output; a setuid-copied binary could not be exercised for privilege escalation since noexec already blocks execution on the same mounts.

evidence.requirement: device nodes are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: A character device node (mknod c 1 3) was created on both /tmp and /dev/shm; attempting to open/read it via cat failed with exit 1 on both, directly proving nodev enforcement (not just the mount flag).

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol for node1
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (f0f8b8e0...) and healthy hardened-mount state, issued a backgrounded shutdown -r now whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, observed the node briefly unreachable, then confirmed a new boot_id (50e13c78...) with ~7.7s uptime, and re-verified /tmp and /dev/shm hardening and enforcement post-reboot.

attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), hardened /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev, made the settings persistent, verified enforcement, rebooted the node, and confirmed the hardening survived the reboot.
